- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to correct downward.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the middle-to-late forecast period, suggesting mean reversion is not captured well.
- Lags in response to recent price drops — model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward after a true decline.
- Tends to overreact to minor price volatility, producing erratic peaks and troughs in the forecast, especially in the last 5–10 days.
- Underestimates the magnitude of price recovery after a dip — often fails to recognize that prices rebound faster than modeled.
- Forecasts are overly smooth, missing short-term volatility spikes and troughs that occur within the last 7–10 days of history.
